one_liner: AI meeting assistant for transcription, summaries, and conversation insights
blocker: Public API is restricted to Enterprise workspaces and must be enabled by an Otter account manager

evidence.claim: API access is Enterprise-only and enabled via account manager (gated)
evidence.quote: Yes, Otter offers a public API for Enterprise customers. To get started, contact your Otter account manager to enable access.

evidence.claim: Authentication uses an API key sent as a Bearer token
evidence.quote: All API requests require authentication using Bearer token authentication. Follow the steps below to create your **API key.**

evidence.claim: REST API covers channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details
evidence.quote: Otter.ai's Public API provides programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details from your Otter account.

evidence.claim: API requires the Otter Enterprise plan and possibly admin permissions
evidence.quote: This content is available for the **Otter Enterprise** plan and may require admin permissions.

evidence.claim: Vendor documents an official Otter MCP Server, but setup requires contacting Otter Support
evidence.quote: We currently do not have a public API key at this time. Contact our Otter Support Team for help setting up Otter MCP with your AI application.

notes: Official MCP server article exists on help.otter.ai, but onboarding is manual via Otter Support (no public API key for MCP). API keys are self-serve once Enterprise is enabled (Account Settings > Developer, limit of 2 keys per user, key shown once). Rate limit is 10 requests/second; webhooks are supported and recommended over polling. Beware name collision: helpdesk.tryotter.com 'API Documentation' result is a different company (restaurant ordering platform), not Otter.ai. Zapier integration also uses the same Developer API key.
